caveats: ⚑ skill2 trigger cadence: kit says 'when performing a Full Charge attack' — modeled as chargeCounter count:1 (every full charge). Yan is RL with chargeFrames 90; the datamined cadence tuple (reloadFrames 141, ammo 6, chargeFrames 90) is a known-unreliable datamine field, so the resulting re-application rate (and therefore the 5s buff's real uptime) is UNMEASURED.

⚑ skill2 uptime: the 5s window vs the full-charge interval decides whether the ATK/crit buff is effectively permanent or duty-cycled. If the effective charge cycle exceeds 5s the buff lapses between shots; unmeasured either way.

⚑ burst damage: modeled as instant on-cast (no flight time). RL burst nukes elsewhere in the roster have measured flight delay; if popup footage shows the hit landing inside the Full Burst window, add delaySec and drop noFb.
⚑ burst crit: the 348.73% hit is modeled crit-eligible at the caster's sheet rate (roster default for burst damage) and core-ineligible (kit says no 'core strike'). Unmeasured for this unit.
Burst-cast damage is FB-exempt by convention (a burst cast lands before the Full Burst window opens) — noFb:true here follows that rule, not a per-unit measurement.

'Forced movement toward the center of attack range' is a boss-positioning effect; the scope-lock boss has a scripted range/movement profile the engine owns, so this line has no representable primitive.
override.note: PARSER BASELINE (HYPOTHESIS — NOT a validated model). Every ⚑ below is an UNMEASURED estimate; hand-tune + record against a real fight before trusting any number. Yan (RL/Fire/Supporter/Burst I) is a pure charge-support buffer plus one burst nuke. S1 is a team-wide Charge Damage ▲21.55%/10s keyed to Full Burst entry (fullBurstEnter — the kit says 'at the beginning of Full Burst', which fires on ANY team Full Burst, not only rotations Yan bursts); chargeDamagePct is the additive charge-bucket stat, not chargeDamageMultPct (the kit line is a plain 'Charge Damage ▲ x%', not a 'damage multiplier scaled by' line). S2 is a team-wide ATK ▲2.77% + Critical Rate ▲1.33% for 5s re-applied on each of Yan's own full-charge attacks; the crit line is UNSCOPED in the kit text (no 'of normal attacks' qualifier) so it is generic critRatePct, not critRateNormalPct. Burst deals 348.73% of final ATK to enemies in range as an instant on-cast hit, FB-exempt per the burst-cast convention. The forced-movement clause is unmodeled: the sim owns boss position via a measured range script, so a kit-driven reposition has no primitive and would collide with measured ground truth.

flags.estimate: chargeCounter {count: 1} — one activation per full-charge attack
flags.reasoning: The kit gives an activation clause ('when performing a Full Charge attack') but no cadence. The RESULTING re-application rate depends entirely on the datamined cadence tuple (chargeFrames 90 ≈ 1.5s charge, ammo 6, reloadFrames 141 ≈ 2.35s), and rate_of_fire/reloadFrames are the known-unreliable datamine fields. So the trigger IDENTITY is certain from the text; its FREQUENCY — and therefore whether the 5s ATK/crit window ever lapses — is not.
flags.recipe: Focus-record Yan firing continuously; count full-charge releases per 10s from the ammo counter / charge-release audio-visual cue and compare against the engine's chargeCounter fire log (DBG_UNIT=yan with a chargeCounter tap). If measured releases occur more often than every 5s, the buffs are effectively permanent and only the ramp-in matters.

flags.recipe: Ammo-counter read from a focus recording: count shots per magazine and time reload-start → first-shot to get effective reload; time charge-start → release for the effective charge window (respecting 60fps frame quantization, effective = 60/ceil(60/nominal)).

flags.reasoning: The text says 'at the beginning of Full Burst', which is the full-burst-enter wording, not 'when using Burst Skill'. Yan is Burst I, so a burstCast keying would fire at her own B1 cast — before the FB window — and the 10s Charge Damage window would start ~1.5s early, partially wasting it. Trigger identity is textually clear; noting it because burstCast/fullBurstEnter divergence is the taxonomy's #3 trap and the two are only distinguishable in multi-caster comps.
